messages.subject: do.neishabouricounts
parts:
Hi Jiaro and Vincent,

I have a question regarding do.neishabouricounts and if I understand this correct that this function converts raw data in counts comparable to what actilife does, do you need to specify cut-off points to identify intensity levels?

If yes, should these cut-points be cut-off points in mg such as Hildebrand or should I use cut-off points in cpm such as Freedson?

Thanks in advance for your time!

Kind regards,
Iris

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] do.neishabouricounts
parts:
Hi Iris,

I think you can use outpoints in cpm as in ActiLife.

I have not done this myself yet, so would be good to hear whether you get plausible values.

There is a possibility that the cut-points needs to be adjusted to account for the fact that your GGIR epochs are possibly 5 seconds, while the cut-points are per minute. So, maybe we need to divide or multiply by 12 (60/5). Can you try it out and report back whether output is plausible? I am a bit busy at the moment to test this myself.

Vincent

parts:
Hi Vincent,

Thanks for responding. I tested this but If have some additional questions. 

So if I want to use the cut-point from Sasaki et al. (Freedson V3) than the following cut-points are proposed:

  • Lpa <2690,
  • MPA 2691-6166,
  • VPA > 6166

These cut-points were established at 60 sec epochs at 30 hz wearing the Actigraph on the hip.

As I work with Actigraphs worn on the hip and I use 60 sec epochs at 100 hz. I think I need to convert these values?
  • I recorded at 6000 data points per epoch (60sec x 100 hz)
  • Sasaki recorded at 1800 datapoints per epoch (60 sec x 30 hz)
  • So do I need to cutpoint/60*18 ?
  • LPA< 807 cpm
  • MPA 808-1849 cpm
  • VPA: >1949 cpm.
1) But with these cutpoints we do not have a SB-LPA treshhold which we need to define in GGIR to distinguish LPA from SB. Most cpm are using 100 or 150 cpm to define the threshold form SB to LPA however, these were calculated for vertical axis devices and not for vector magnitude. Do you have any suggestions how to define this cut-point? 
When using the above mentioned cut points - I get a potential underestimation of MVPA then when I check I manually with Actilife.

2) In addition, if GGIR uses epochs from 5 sec but I initialized my actigraph at 60 sec and used cutpoints validated on 60 sec epochs, should I still divide the the cut points by 12? This create very low cut points which does not seem correct

3) If I use do.neishabouricounts, I assume I should specify do.enmo=FALSE as I I think Actilife data is not rounded to zero?

Thanks for helping me.

Kind regards,
Iris

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] do.neishabouricounts
parts: Hi Iris,

Thanks for responding. I tested this but If have some additional questions.

So if I want to use the cut-point from Sasaki et al. (Freedson V3) than the following cut-points are proposed:

  • Lpa <2690,
  • MPA 2691-6166,
  • VPA > 6166

These cut-points were established at 60 sec epochs at 30 hz wearing the Actigraph on the hip.

As I work with Actigraphs worn on the hip and I use 60 sec epochs at 100 hz. I think I need to convert these values?
  • I recorded at 6000 data points per epoch (60sec x 100 hz)
  • Sasaki recorded at 1800 datapoints per epoch (60 sec x 30 hz)
  • So do I need to cutpoint/60*18 ?
  • LPA< 807 cpm
  • MPA 808-1849 cpm
  • VPA: >1949 cpm.

You should not incorporate the sample rate difference, because this is already accounted in the count calculation. Instead, only look at epoch length, which is identical if you use 60 second epochs. So, I think no correction is needed if cut-points in ActiLife are used at 60 second epoch level. If you would use 5 second epoch in GGIR then the correction would be to divide by 12 (or multiple by 0.08333).

1) But with these cutpoints we do not have a SB-LPA treshhold which we need to define in GGIR to distinguish LPA from SB. Most cpm are using 100 or 150 cpm to define the threshold form SB to LPA however, these were calculated for vertical axis devices and not for vector magnitude. Do you have any suggestions how to define this cut-point?
When using the above mentioned cut points - I get a potential underestimation of MVPA then when I check I manually with Actilife.

do.neishabouricounts = TRUE
acc.metric = "NeishabouriCount_y"

should give you time spent based on cut-points derived with the y-axis.
I now see that this "NeishabouriCount_y" is not well documented yet, will add it to the to do list.

2) In addition, if GGIR uses epochs from 5 sec but I initialized my actigraph at 60 sec and used cutpoints validated on 60 sec epochs, should I still divide the the cut points by 12? This create very low cut points which does not seem correct
Yes, but do not apply the sample frequency conversion you mentioned above.
3) If I use do.neishabouricounts, I assume I should specify do.enmo=FALSE as I I think Actilife data is not rounded to zero?

Yes, you can set it to FALSE, because the cut-points you specify are only meaningful for ActiLife counts. Rounding to zero is only worth considering for metrics that do vector minus one gravity, and not relevant to filter-based metrics as ActiLife counts, BFEN, HFEN, and similar.

Best, Vincent


Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] do.neishabouricounts
parts:
Hi Vincent,

Thank you for the explanation and your help.

I tested the do.neishabouri with Freedson cut-points (VA) or Troiano cut-points (VA) using the NeishabouriCount_y metric. Moreover I specify part5_agg2_60sec=TRUE to create epoch of 60 seconds instead of 5 seconds.

1)      Troiano (VA): vertical axis, 60s, 10hz

LPA: 101 cpm

MPA: 2020 cpm

VPA: 5998 cpm

2)      Freedson (VA): vertical axis, 60s, 30 hz

LPA: 100 cpm

MPA: 760 cpm

VPA: 5724 cpm


I used the cut-points without adjustments as you mentioned above but this gives non-realistic output (only 30 min LPA and no MVPA). 
I tried the cut-points when dividing them by 12. However I do specify part5_agg2_60sec=TRUE so this does not sound logical to do. When dividing by 12,  the output was again a bit odd with very high levels of MVPA (not realistic for the tested population).

So I tried to adjust the cut-points for frequency (hz) and this gave me output more or less in line with the expectations. However, as you said it is not necessary to adjust for frequency I am not sure this is right way to do it.

Kind regards,
Iris Willems
